# Results -- Study 509 (Intermediate-Momentum) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: monthly equal-weight
dollar-neutral momentum long-shorts (top tercile minus bottom tercile) built on two formation
windows -- **intermediate** (t-12..t-7) and **recent** (t-6..t-1) -- over a large-cap survivor
basket, with one execution lag, turnover-based costs + short borrow, a label-shuffle placebo,
and a synthetic positive control. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 4780 days x 46 tickers | `e21fc3ab636a` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 4780 days | `11cdeebb16d8` |
| Period covered | 2007-01-03 -- 2025-12-31 (complete years) | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True). Universe: 46 large-cap
US names (a stable 48-name candidate list, 2 dropped for thin coverage). The panel is
survivorship-biased -- current large-cap members projected backwards.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** only companies still trading in 2026 are in the
sample. Past losers that were delisted -- the natural short candidates for a momentum sort --
have been removed. All results are **upper-bound estimates**.

## The honest test -- intermediate vs recent momentum

At each month-end, every stock's formation-window return is computed from daily prices: the
**intermediate** window is the cumulative return over months t-12..t-7; the **recent** window
is months t-6..t-1 (the most recent month is skipped to avoid short-term reversal). The
cross-section is ranked; we go long the top tercile and short the bottom tercile, enter
one trading day after the signal (one execution lag), and hold one calendar month.

| Statistic | Intermediate (t-12..t-7) | Recent (t-6..t-1) |
|---|---|---|
| N months | 215 (2008-01 -- 2025-12) | 221 (2007-07 -- 2025-12) |
| Mean return (annualised, gross) | **-0.31%/yr** | **+0.25%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 11.46%/yr | 12.17%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.027 | +0.021 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-0.121** | **+0.090** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 48.8% | 54.3% |
| Max drawdown | -48.4% | -52.9% |

- The intermediate long-short earns **-0.31%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-0.121** -- statistically
  indistinguishable from zero, and (if anything) negative.
- The recent long-short earns **+0.25%/yr** at HAC *t* = **+0.090** -- also indistinguishable
  from zero.
- **Neither window clears the |t| >= 2 bar.** On this large-cap survivor basket the Novy-Marx
  (2012) prediction -- that the intermediate window carries the drift while the recent window
  does not -- does not reproduce: both are flat, and the intermediate window is marginally the
  *worse* of the two.

## Placebo null (label-shuffle)

We re-run each sort but randomly permute which stocks are "winners" vs "losers" at every
rebalance (200 shuffles), preserving the return distribution and holding mechanics while
destroying the signal. The p-value is the share of shuffles whose mean long-short return
matches or beats the real mean.

| Window | Real mean (per month) | Placebo p-value |
|---|---|---|
| Intermediate | -0.026% | **0.565** |
| Recent | +0.021% | **0.400** |

Both real sorts sit squarely inside their shuffle distributions -- the real labels carry no
information the random ones lack.

## Costs and turnover

One-way 5 bps per leg-side, charged on turnover (each leg is entered and exited), plus 50 bps
annual borrow on the short leg.

| Window | Avg turnover | Gross (ann) | Net (ann) | Net HAC t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intermediate | 28.7% | -0.31%/yr | **-1.50%/yr** | -0.59 |
| Recent | 28.6% | +0.25%/yr | **-0.94%/yr** | -0.34 |

Costs push both already-flat sorts firmly negative.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness)

A deterministic offline panel where a known momentum premium is planted **only** in the
intermediate window. A faithful engine should find the drift in the intermediate sort and
*not* in the recent sort, with the intermediate *t* rising in the planted premium.

| Planted premium | Intermediate mean (t) | Recent mean (t) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.00 (null) | +0.66%/yr (t=+0.27) | -2.90%/yr (t=-1.30) |
| 0.06 | +7.74%/yr (t=+3.37) | -3.15%/yr (t=-1.33) |
| 0.12 | +14.29%/yr (t=+6.26) | -4.15%/yr (t=-1.78) |

The engine recovers the planted intermediate premium monotonically (*t* climbs 0.27 -> 3.37
-> 6.26) and leaves the recent sort flat. So the null result on the real tape reflects **the
market**, not a broken detector.

A choppy, signless ride: strong crisis-era years (2008, 2011) offset by a long stretch of
weak-to-negative years from 2018 onward (the well-documented post-2010 momentum drought).

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Intermediate HAC *t* = -0.121, recent HAC *t* = +0.090; both inside
  their placebo distributions (p = 0.57 / 0.40). Neither window carries a drift the tape can
  distinguish from zero on this 18-year large-cap survivor basket. Literature (Novy-Marx 2012)
  documents the intermediate effect on a broad CRSP universe; it does not survive on 46
  large-cap survivors.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Both sorts are flat gross and **negative net** of costs+borrow
  (-1.50%/yr intermediate, -0.94%/yr recent). There is nothing here to monetise.
- **"Does momentum live in the intermediate window?" -- BUSTED (here).** The whole point of
  Novy-Marx (2012) is that the intermediate sort should beat the recent one. On this basket it
  does not -- the intermediate sort is, if anything, marginally *worse*. The horizon
  decomposition that holds on the broad CRSP cross-section dissolves on a 46-name large-cap
  survivor universe.
